0,3,1: Week 1 - ICP and the shift to retained advisory
0,4,1:
George Berrington (BeDeveloped)
Joanna Pike (Managing Partner)
Oliver Grant (Head of Practice)
1,0,1: George Berrington ran the opening session with Joanna Pike and Oliver Grant to define who Larkspur should be selling to as it moves from one-off projects to retained advisory. We agreed the core ICP is mid-market PE-backed businesses going through a buy-and-build, with the PE operating partner as the economic buyer. Pricing for a retainer was discussed but not settled.
5,1,1: Turn the buy-and-build ICP into a value proposition and commercial narrative for operating partners.
5,2,1: Joanna to bring two recent integration project write-ups that show measurable outcomes.
2,1,1: Joanna said roughly 70% of last year's fee income came from one-off leadership assessments, mostly corporates with no repeat work. Oliver noted the post-deal integration projects were smaller in number but far more likely to lead to follow-on work.
2,2,1: Both agreed the people who rehire them are PE operating partners and portfolio CHROs, not the HR directors of standalone corporates. Joanna was worried that narrowing the focus would cut off the corporate assessment work that pays the bills today.
2,3,1: Oliver felt operating partners would pay a monthly fee for on-call people advice across a portfolio, but had no evidence yet. Joanna wants to test it with three existing PE relationships before committing.
3,1,1: Define the primary ICP as PE-backed businesses with 150 to 1,500 employees in a buy-and-build phase, with the PE operating partner as economic buyer.
3,2,1: Split the market into three segments: PE portfolio buy-and-build, mid-market PE houses at fund level, and standalone corporates, with corporates treated as a secondary segment only.
3,3,1: Position Larkspur as the people integration partner for the first 18 months after a deal, rather than a generalist HR consultancy.
3,7,1: Introduce a portfolio people retainer at 6,500 GBP per month covering up to 4 portfolio companies.
3,5,1: Map the five Bristol and London boutiques that pitch to the same operating partners before the Week 2 session.
4,1,0: List the top 12 PE operating partner relationships and rate each on retainer potential
4,2,0: Send the three-segment market map to the partners for comment
